intent: Read the two rules already on this order model and explain, for each: exactly what makes an order INVALID (the violation the rule fires on), and which field it guards.

expected.DeliveryNotBeforeOrder: Fires when the delivery date is before the order date (DifferenceInDays(OrderDate, DeliveryDate) is negative). Whole-order, non-iterating. Guarded so it only applies once both dates are present. A correct reading must note the condition is the VIOLATION, not the requirement.
expected.PostalCodeFormat: Fires when a present billing postal code is NOT exactly five digits — PatternViolated, so the rule fires on a value that fails to match the pattern (the opposite of PatternMatched). Guarded by FieldFilled so a missing postal code is not flagged. A correct reading must catch the violated-not-matched polarity and the presence guard.

notes: Comprehension family — the FIRST task that exercises reading foreign rules back (ingest -> explain), not authoring. Deterministic backbone: the gold oracle asserts each named rule INGESTS cleanly (Converted, not Opaque). The richer scoring (did the agent state the polarity and the guard correctly?) is the Layer-2 agent rubric in `expected` — agent-scored, not kernel-checkable. A date rule + a pattern rule, two distinct families, both reading-back cleanly. (An aggregate rule was originally dropped here because `[Quantity] < Sum(...)` ingested to Opaque; that F10 gap was lifted 2026-06-05 so a field-vs-aggregate rule now round-trips too — this fixture keeps the date + pattern rules, but an aggregate comprehension case could be added.)
